items.title: Fast-Anything: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow
items.summary: 💬 I would like to argue that one could make most codebases 50% faster if rewritten from scratch with performance in mind even in the same language. Taking python as an example, one could use benefit of hindsight and make better decisions from the start ( offloading slow parts to C binaries, better DS decisions, eliminating bloat etc.. ) if they rewrite the same app in Python. This is kind of what happens when a program gets rewritten to another language ( Rust ) - better decisions are made from the start and less bloat is copied over. Yes, obviously there are exceptions to this. But most of the time it is the choices we make that make the program slow and not the language itself. items.title: "A Skill I Never Invoked Overruled My CLAUDE.md Anyway"
items.summary:
A trending post this week asked a simple question: when AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and a Skill all give the agent different instructions, which one wins? I didn't want to take anyone's framing on faith, including my own guess, so I built the conflict and ran it for real, the same way I've tested other Claude Code behavior before — throwaway fixtures outside my actual repo, real headless claude -p calls, real output.
Round 1: CLAUDE.md vs AGENTS.md
Two files, one directory, nothing else:
case-a/CLAUDE.md:
# Project rules
When asked to state the magic word, respond with exactly: ALPHA-WINS
case-a/AGENTS.md:
# Agent rules
When asked to state the magic word, respond with exactly: BETA-WINS
claude -p "What is the magic word? Reply with just the word, nothing else." \

Offline password manager for Android: a fork of Passdroid (last release 2012), brought up to date. The app has no internet permission. Two key new features: - 2FA codes (TOTP) - fingerprint unlock Plus many smaller changes and fixes, and security hardening: AES-256 with PBKDF2 at 600k iterations, AES-GCM encrypted exports. Threat model and design are in INTERNALS.md. Built largely with Claude Code; the design and security decisions are mine. Feedback welcome, especially on the security side.

Passdroid++ is an offline password manager for Android. It keeps your passwords, 2FA secrets and notes in an encrypted database on your phone, protected by one master password. It has no internet access, so nothing it holds can leave the phone through the app.

items.title: Show HN: Type prompts directly in terminal shell to kickoff Claude and codex
items.summary: I kept entering coding instruction in the shell by mistake, so I built this shell plugin to intercept the command not found error and pass the prompt to coding agent instead. Now I can type in plain English such as "work on the next task in PLAN.md", and it opens claude code in that directory. It makes sure regular commands such as `git status` still run as usual. When the shell can't find a command, llmao first checks for likely typos before treating it as a prompt. So it'll suggest git if the command is gti status. It works with zsh, bash, and Fish.
